title: Sliding puzzles
description: A sliding puzzle's start/goal shapes and the starts and goals stamped on them (decision 0014; the original's Start/Goal tab). A start/goal shape is a tray: its empty cells are walls, its variable cells corridors a piece may cross but not stop on (both edited with shape.setCells); each piece may have a start and a goal on it, the whole piece at a time. Trays and pieces may be more than one layer deep: a stamp marks every cell of its piece, and on a tray of several layers a piece may also move up and down as it slides. Each start/goal shape has a problem of its own (named START/GOAL n), whose parts and colour locks follow its stamps; the shape commands keep the stamps in step (shape.delete, shape.move, shape.duplicate, shape.rename, and an edit that changes a piece's shape takes its stamps off). Refused (unsupported) on other grids.

sliding.addStartGoal.summary: Adds a start/goal shape (the original's New Start/Goal) of 'size' cells (default 6 by 6 by 1, the original took the selected shape's; a size [x, y] is one layer), all floor, numbered after the others, with its problem.

sliding.place.summary: The start/goal editor's click: the whole of a piece as its start (goal false) or its goal, placed from a click on cell 'at' (y rises upwards, as in the grid editor): the piece's slice on that layer with its top-left cell there, at the lowest height that puts a layer of the piece on that layer and fits (on a tray of one layer, the piece's top-left cell there), moved there if it was elsewhere; a piece that is exactly there already is taken off. Refused (invalid_argument) with the original's reason when it does not fit: off the floor, on another piece's start or goal, a goal on a corridor. The problems of the start/goal shape lose what they had found. One undo step.

placed.description: The piece is there now (false: it was there and was taken off).

sliding.clearAt.summary: Takes off the start or goal that covers a cell (the editor's right click). One undo step; nothing when none covers it.

sliding.tray.summary: What a start/goal shape holds: its number and name, each cell's start and goal (the piece stamped there, cells indexed x + X*(y + Y*z)), whether it can be solved (the original's validity bar: null, or why not), the stamps larger than their pieces (null, or the message), and its floor cells.

name.description: The user's part of its name; shown as '(START/GOAL n) name'.

sliding.preview.summary: Where sliding.place would put a piece: the cells, every layer (when no height fits, the lowest that puts a layer of the piece on the layer of 'at'; none when no layer of the piece can be there), whether it fits (and the original's reason when not), and whether it is exactly there already (then the click takes it off). Changes nothing.

TrayCell.description: A cell [x, y, z] of a start/goal shape, y up; [x, y] is on its first layer (z = 0).

TraySize.description: A size [x, y, z] in cells; [x, y] is one layer.
